package_info.package_manager: malicious Windows executable (delivered via Microsoft Word OLE object)
package_info.why_malicious: AstraLocker 2.0 is ransomware that encrypts user files, deletes backups, disables security tools, and demands cryptocurrency payment for decryption. It is delivered via phishing emails containing malicious Microsoft Word documents with embedded executables. Upon execution, it immediately performs anti-analysis checks, disables system defenses, deletes recovery options, and encrypts files across local and network drives, resulting in data loss and extortion.

execution_context.trigger: user double-clicks embedded executable in Word document
execution_context.file_location: OLE object inside malicious Microsoft Word document

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When the user double-clicks the embedded executable, the code checks for virtual machine environments, sandbox analysis, and running analysis tools, then terminates if any are detected, preventing execution in analysis environments and evading detection.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Checking for virtual machines, sandboxes, or analysis tools and terminating if found is a well-known anti-analysis and evasion technique used by malware to avoid detection and analysis. Legitimate software rarely implements such checks except in very specific contexts.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal applications do not attempt to evade security analysis or terminate themselves based on the presence of analysis environments or tools.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some DRM or licensing software may check for VMs to prevent piracy, but such checks are not expected in standard productivity or user applications, especially not in executables embedded in Word documents.
key_indicators: Environment checks for VM or sandbox presence
Process or window name checks for analysis tools
Conditional self-termination on detection of analysis environment

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: for each service in [backup, anti-malware]: stopService(service); for each process in [interfering_processes]: killProcess(process);
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Immediately after initial execution, the code iterates through a list of backup and anti-malware services, stopping each one, and then kills processes that could interfere with file encryption, thereby disabling system defenses and increasing the likelihood of successful ransomware execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Disabling security and backup services is a hallmark of ransomware, as it maximizes the impact of the attack by preventing recovery and detection. This behavior is highly suspicious in any context outside of legitimate maintenance or uninstallation routines.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software should not indiscriminately stop or kill unrelated security or backup services and processes.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate uninstallers may stop their own services during removal, but they do not target unrelated security or backup services.
key_indicators: Bulk termination of backup and anti-malware services
Killing processes associated with system defense or recovery

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Before encrypting files, the code deletes all volume shadow copies and empties the recycle bin, removing local backup and recovery options to ensure that victims cannot restore their files without paying the ransom.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Deleting shadow copies and emptying the recycle bin are classic ransomware tactics to prevent victims from recovering their files using built-in Windows recovery features.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal applications do not delete system backups or empty the recycle bin without explicit user consent, especially not as part of their standard operation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Disk cleanup utilities may empty the recycle bin, but they do not delete shadow copies without clear user approval and notification.
key_indicators: Programmatic deletion of volume shadow copies
Automated emptying of the recycle bin
Removal of local file recovery options

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: for each drive in enumerateDrivesAndShares(): mount(drive); for each file in drive: encryptFile(file, curve25519_key);
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During the main encryption phase, the code enumerates and mounts all local drives and network shares, then iterates through each file, encrypting it using Curve25519 elliptic curve cryptography, resulting in all user data becoming inaccessible without the decryption key.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Bulk enumeration and encryption of files across all drives and network shares is the core behavior of ransomware, designed to maximize the impact and force victims to pay for decryption.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not encrypt user files or network shares with unknown keys without explicit user intent and consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Backup software may access and copy files, but it does not encrypt them with unknown or inaccessible keys.
key_indicators: Enumeration and mounting of all drives and network shares
Bulk file encryption using strong ECC (Curve25519)
Automated processing of user and shared files

attack_chain.action: User receives phishing email with malicious Word document and opens it.
User double-clicks the OLE-embedded executable, launching the ransomware payload.
Ransomware checks for VM, sandbox, and analysis tools; exits if detected.
Ransomware stops backup and anti-malware services, kills interfering processes.
attack_chain.leads_to: Deletes shadow copies and empties recycle bin.

attack_chain.action: Ransomware deletes volume shadow copies and empties the recycle bin.
attack_chain.leads_to: Enumerates and mounts drives and network shares.

attack_chain.action: Ransomware enumerates and mounts all drives and network shares.
Ransomware encrypts files on all accessible drives and network shares.
attack_chain.leads_to: Files are inaccessible; ransom note is displayed.

behavioral_signatures: Executable launched from OLE object embedded in Office document
Immediate anti-VM, anti-sandbox, and anti-analysis checks upon execution
Bulk termination of backup and anti-malware services and processes
Programmatic deletion of volume shadow copies
Enumeration and mounting of all local drives and network shares
Bulk file encryption using elliptic curve cryptography (Curve25519)
Creation of ransom note after encryption
file_indicators: Malicious Word documents containing OLE-embedded executables
network_indicators: Possible C2 or payment instructions embedded in ransom note
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Office documents containing OLE-embedded executables, especially those that launch processes upon user interaction. Detect processes that immediately perform anti-VM or anti-analysis checks, stop backup and anti-malware services, delete volume shadow copies, and enumerate or encrypt files across all drives and network shares. Flag files with the .babyk extension and correlate with known malicious hashes. Alert on network activity referencing known cryptocurrency wallet addresses associated with AstraLocker 2.0 ransomware. Look for the creation of ransom notes and sudden, bulk file encryption activity.
